items.title: Man dies following stabbing in Mississauga Saturday morning
items.summary: Peel police were called to a residence near Lakeshore Road East and Fergus Avenue early Saturday morning following reports of an altercation. Officers arrived to find a man suffering from stab wounds and was pronounced dead at the scene. A man is dead after an altercation at a residence in Mississauga early Saturday morning, Peel Regional Police say. m. following reports of an altercation inside a residence. Officers and emergency crews found a man with life-threatening injuries at the scene, Peel police Const. Amanda Steenson told reporters Saturday morning. Emergency responders provided medical assistance, but the man succumbed to his injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene. Any suspect or suspects fled before officers arrived, Steenson said. Police have not released any suspect descriptions, and investigators are still working to determine whether the victim and whoever was responsible knew each other.

items.title: Man dies after stabbing inside Mississauga home
items.summary: A man has died after a stabbing inside a home in Mississauga early Saturday morning. m. on Saturday (Nov. 14). Police say an altercation happened inside the home, and a man was stabbed. He died of his injuries. Police say there is currently no evidence to suggest a threat to public safety. There is a large police presence in the area, and residents are asked to avoid it. Police have not released the man’s identity or age, or said whether anyone has been arrested. Police say more information will be released as it becomes available. Anyone with information is asked to contact Peel Regional Police at 905-453-3311, referencing incident number PR260386225. Anonymous tips can be made to Peel Crime Stoppers at 1-800-222-TIPS (8477).

items.title: No Suspect Description Yet as Peel Police Probe Deadly Stabbing in Mississauga Home
items.summary: According to CTV News Toronto, a man died early Saturday morning after a stabbing inside a residence in Mississauga, and investigators are still working to identify who was involved. Peel Regional Police Const. Amanda Steenson told reporters at the scene that officers and emergency crews gave the victim medical assistance, but he could not be saved. Steenson said police believe the incident was isolated and that there is no broader threat to public safety. She said it is too early to say whether the victim and the person responsible knew each other, and no suspect description has been released, CTV News Toronto reported. Police are asking anyone who was in the area at the time, or who has dashcam or surveillance footage, to come forward, according to the outlet. Investigators have not released further details about what led to the stabbing.

items.title: Could El Niño affect Mississauga services this winter? Here’s what residents need to know about rinks and roads
items.summary: Short, who once voiced the titular character in the animated… From fake salaries to hidden fees — here's how to spot a fra… The weather pattern could delay the opening of Mississauga artificial skating rinks and damage roads and trees this winter. Adults and children skating at the Celebration Square outdoor ice rink. The City of Mississauga is advising residents to prepare for potential municipal service disruptions this fall and winter due to a forecasted strong El Niño weather pattern. El Niño is a natural and global weather pattern which takes place every two to seven years. It’s characterized by warmer-than-average sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean. It brings milder weather to western, northwestern and Central Canada, while Eastern Canada experiences lesser effects, according to the Government of Canada’s website. Due to warmer-than-normal ocean temperatures, which experts say may be intensified due to climate change, a longer, milder fall and slower start to winter is expected in Canada, the city said in an advisory issued on Nov. 12. This means extreme weather and frequent freeze-thaw cycles can be expected in Mississauga, impacting outdoor ice rinks, trees and infrastructure.

items.title: Ontario's Bill 140 raises concerns over landfill approvals, groundwater protection in Caledon, Ont.
items.summary: Ontario's proposed Bill 140 would remove a municipal support requirement for certain large landfills, prompting concerns about groundwater and the time available for Caledon's incoming council to respond.

items.title: Peel Police Launch Festive RIDE Checkstops Through New Year's Eve
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Peel Regional Police kicked off their annual Festive RIDE impaired driving campaign on Friday, with roadside checkstops running across Mississauga and Brampton through New Year's Eve. The outlet reported the program aims to reduce alcohol and drug impaired driving during one of the busiest travel periods of the year. Police said they have investigated more than 35,000 vehicles and conducted nearly 13,000 screening tests since 2024, laying 186 impaired driving charges, insauga.com said. During last year's six week campaign, officers inspected 16,101 vehicles and conducted 6,443 roadside tests, charging 123 people, according to the outlet. That compares with 126 impaired driving charges during the 2024 campaign, insauga.com reported. Peel police said impaired driving remains a leading cause of criminal death in Canada and poses a significant risk to public safety.

items.title: Trixstar's Bankruptcy Filing Leaves Comedy Festival Ticket Holders With Few Options
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Trixstar, the company behind the Great Outdoors Comedy Festival, made an assignment in bankruptcy effective Nov. 13, with MNP Ltd. named as trustee. The outlet reported ticket holders may never recover their money after waiting months for refunds from the festival's cancelled Mississauga debut, postponed just three days before it was set to begin in September. General admission tickets ranged from $39 to $99, while VIP Club tickets reached as much as $499 before fees, insauga.com said. Organizers said at the time they were exploring new dates and would follow up with ticket holders, but no replacement dates were ever announced, according to the outlet. Customers said they could not get answers despite repeated attempts to contact the company, insauga.com reported. With Trixstar now bankrupt, ticket claims must go through the trustee, the outlet said.

items.title: Councillor Sets Up Meetings as CAPREIT Pitches 150-Plus New Townhouses at Two Mississauga Sites
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Ward 3 Councillor Chris Fonseca has scheduled back-to-back community meetings so residents can question developer CAPREIT about two proposed townhouse additions. The outlet reported the plans would add more than 150 townhouses to existing apartment properties at 1055 Bloor Street and 2121 Rathburn Road East. One session will focus on 1055 Bloor Street, where CAPREIT wants to add 112 stacked townhouse units to the existing building, insauga.com said. That proposal already hit a snag in August, when it went before the city's Committee of Adjustment seeking 19 variances. Fonseca said planning staff and committee members raised concerns about parking and traffic impacts, according to the outlet. The committee's staff report recommended deferring the application until the developer worked further with the councillor's office and nearby residents, the outlet reported.

items.title: Francique's Parents Describe Devastating Loss on Opening Day of Peel Police Inquest
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Jamal Francique's parents delivered tearful statements on the first day of the coroner's inquest into his death nearly seven years after Peel police shot him. The outlet reported Derek Francique and Ann-Marie White described their son as a smart, considerate son and devoted father whose loss shattered their family. Derek Francique said his son was always the glue that held their family together and that they are destroyed without him, according to insauga.com. He said the family hopes the inquest brings a fuller understanding of police tactics and whether anti-Black racism played a role in officers' decisions. White said she is not simply grieving a past event but living with the loss and pain every day, the outlet reported. The inquest, which began Friday, is examining the circumstances of Francique's fatal shooting during a 2020 arrest attempt.
